q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
Let me work through this systematically.

## (a) Time left until resolution

Today is 2026-08-13. NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 ends in September 2026, with earnings typically released in late October/early November 2026. Time remaining: approximately 2.5-3 months until the guidance is released.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

NVIDIA has already provided forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 in its May 20, 2026 earnings release: **$91.0 billion ± 2%**, which creates a range of $89.18B to $92.82B.

This guidance is already public. The question asks what NVIDIA's forward guidance will be in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release, which has not yet occurred. However, the research shows the company already issued guidance on May 20, 2026 for this quarter.

The most likely scenario is that actual results reported in the Q2 FY2027 earnings release will fall within or near the $89.18B-$92.82B range that was already guided. Companies typically hit their guidance ranges, especially when they provide a ±2% buffer.

Key context:
- Q1 FY2027 revenue was $81.6B
- Q2 FY2027 guidance is $91.0B (±2%), representing an 11.4% sequential growth
- This guidance already exceeds analyst consensus of $86.84B
- The company explicitly assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- Worse-than-expected AI demand or customer delays
- Macro deterioration between May and Q2 earnings release
- China export restrictions tightening further
- Competitive pressures from AMD or other competitors
- Inventory corrections at major customers
- However, given the ±2% guidance cushion, actual results are unlikely to fall below ~$89.2B unless there's a significant shock

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Stronger-than-expected GPU demand from cloud providers
- Better conversion of orders into revenue
- Upside surprises in non-Data Center segments
- China restrictions relaxing (though guidance assumes zero China DC revenue, so relaxation would be pure upside)
- Market share gains from competitors
- The ±2% buffer already suggests management confidence they can exceed lower end

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

From the research: NVIDIA's Q1 FY2027 revenue was $81.6B. Q2 FY2027 guidance is $91.0B ± 2%.

The company's own guidance (from their May 20, 2026 earnings release) provides the most relevant anchor. NVIDIA typically guides conservatively and meets its guidance ranges. The ±2% range is relatively tight, suggesting high confidence.

## Analysis

The question asks for NVIDIA's forward guidance that will appear in the Q2 FY2027 earnings release. The guidance has already been provided ($91.0B ± 2%), but the question is asking what the actual reported revenue will be when Q2 results are announced.

Given:
- Official guidance: $91.0B ± 2% ($89.18B - $92.82B)
- NVIDIA's track record of meeting guidance
- The ±2% buffer suggesting management confidence
- 2.5-3 months until results, which is not much time for dramatic changes

The distribution should be centered around $91.0B with most probability mass within the guidance range. Some tail risk for both upside (if demand accelerates) and downside (if there are unexpected disruptions), but the guidance range ($89.18B-$92.82B) should capture the vast majority of probability.

The provided forecast range is $99.5B-$115.5B, which extends well above the company's own guidance. This suggests the question may be asking about something different, but the research clearly shows the May 2026 guidance was $91.0B ± 2%.

q_45367.research_text: NVIDIA provided its outlook for the second quarter of fiscal 2027 in its Q1 FY2027 earnings release on May 20, 2026. The company expects revenue to be $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%. This guidance is well above the LSEG average quarterly revenue estimate of $86.84 billion [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html). NVIDIA's Q1 FY2027 revenue was $81.6 billion, up 20% from the previous quarter and 85% from a year ago [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). Notably, the company is not assuming any Data Center compute revenue from China in its Q2 FY2027 outlook [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html). Gross margins are anticipated to be 74.9% (GAAP) and 75.0% (non-GAAP), plus or minus 50 basis points. Operating expenses are projected to be approximately $8.5 billion (GAAP) and $8.3 billion (non-GAAP) [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027/).
